definition: Yooreeka is a library for data mining, machine learning, soft computing, and mathematical analysis.
details: The project started with the code of the book "Algorithms of the Intelligent Web". Although the term "Web" prevailed in the title, in essence, the algorithms are valuable in any software application. It covers all major algorithms and provides many examples. Yooreeka 2.x is licensed under the Apache License rather than the somewhat more restrictive LGPL (which was the license of v1.x). The library is written 100% in the Java language.

explainer.lead: Yooreeka is a Java library for data mining, machine learning, soft computing and mathematical analysis. It packages many major algorithms with worked examples rather than a single method.

tiers.eli5: It's a toolbox of ready-made algorithms you can pick from, with examples showing how each one works.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a Java reference and implementation base for data mining and ML tasks. A pitfall is version licensing: 2.x is Apache-licensed, while 1.x used the more restrictive LGPL.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a library rather than a single model, so no formal definition applies; its scope covers data mining, machine learning, soft computing and mathematical analysis, with the known limit that licensing changed between major versions.

explainer.example: A developer building a Java application uses Yooreeka's examples to add a recommendation or clustering routine without writing the algorithm from scratch.
